_about: Representative NASA reference imagery per world, used to tune the texture palettes in assets/worldgen/worlds.py. Imagery credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech and partner institutions; most NASA imagery is public domain (see https://www.nasa.gov/multimedia/guidelines/).

reference.title: Graben on the Moon
reference.description: These graben - a kind of trench that is formed as a surface expands - were imaged near a region of the Moon called Mare Frigoris by NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO).  https://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA23237

reference.title: Occator on Ceres Limb
reference.description: This image of the limb of dwarf planet Ceres shows a section of the northern hemisphere. Prominently featured is Occator Crater, home of Ceres' intriguing brightest areas. reference.title: Dawn Soars Over Asteroid Vesta in 3-D
reference.description: This 3D image was obtained as Dawn approached Vesta and circled the giant asteroid during the mission survey orbit phase. You need 3D glasses to view this image.

reference.title: Viking Lander 1 U.S. Flag on Mars Surface
reference.description: Viking Lander 1 U.S. Flag on Mars Surface

reference.title: Global Callisto in Color
reference.description: Bright scars on a darker surface testify to a long history of impacts on Jupiter moon Callisto in this image of Callisto from NASA Galileo spacecraft.

reference.title: Lumps Within Ganymede
reference.description: This mosaic of Jupiter’s moon Ganymede consists of more than 100 images acquired with NASA’s Voyager and Galileo spacecrafts, showing irregular lumps beneath the icy surface.

reference.title: Europa Active Surface
reference.description: On June 27, 1996, during Galileo first orbit around Jupiter, a newly discovered impact crater could be seen just right of the center of this image of Jupiter moon Europa returned by NASA Galileo spacecraft camera.  http://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00294

reference.title: Galileo Near-Infrared Mapping Spectrometer Detects Active Lava Flows at Prometheus Volcano, Io
reference.description: The active volcano Prometheus on Jupiter moon Io was imaged by NASA Galileo spacecraft during the close flyby of Io on Oct.10, 1999. The spectrometer can detect active volcanoes on Io by measuring their heat in the near-infrared wavelengths.

reference.title: Craters Before Haze
reference.description: NASA Cassini spacecraft views the cratered surface of Saturn moon Tethys in front of the hazy orb of the planet largest moon, Titan. Tethys is much closer than Titan to Cassini.

reference.title: Tiger Stripes are Cubs
reference.description: This visual and infrared mapping spectrometer image captured by NASA Cassini spacecraft of Saturn moon Enceladus, shows the dark cracks at the south pole dubbed tiger stripes for their distinct stripe-like appearance.

reference.title: Triton - Detail of Dark and Light Material
reference.description: NASA's Voyager 2 acquired this black and white image of Triton, Neptune's largest satellite, during the night of Aug. 24-25, 1989. reference.title: Contrasting Crescents
reference.description: In this view, Saturn's icy moon Rhea passes in front of Titan as seen by NASA's Cassini spacecraft. Some of the differences between the two large moons are readily apparent. reference.title: Farewell to Iapetus
reference.description: Cassini bids farewell to Saturn's yin-and-yang moon, Iapetus. This image is from the last set of observations Cassini made of this world of striking contrasts. reference.title: Half-lit Dione
reference.description: Saturn's moon Dione is captured in this view from NASA's Cassini spacecraft, half in shadow and half in light. reference.title: Uranus - Montage of Uranus Five Largest Satellites
reference.description: Montage of Uranus five largest satellites taken by NASA Voyager 2. From to right to left in order of decreasing distance from Uranus are Oberon, Titania, Umbriel, Ariel, and Miranda.

reference.title: Oberon at Voyager Closest Approach
reference.description: This image of Oberon, Uranus outermost moon, was captured by NASA Voyager 2 on Jan. 24, 1986. Clearly visible are several large impact craters in Oberon icy surface surrounded by bright rays.  http://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00034

reference.title: Umbriel at Closest Approach
reference.description: The southern hemisphere of Umbriel displays heavy cratering in this NASA Voyager 2 image, taken Jan. 24, 1986. This frame is the most detailed image of Umbriel, the darkest of Uranus larger moons.  http://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00040

reference.title: Ariel at Voyager Closest Approach
reference.description: This picture is part of NASA Voyager 2 imaging sequence of Ariel, a moon of Uranus taken on January 24, 1986. The complexity of Ariel surface indicates that a variety of geologic processes have occurred.  http://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00037

reference.title: Miranda Icy Face
reference.description: Uranus icy moon Miranda is seen in this image from Voyager 2 on January 24, 1986.  https://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA18185

reference.title: New Horizons Sees Pluto
reference.description: The Long Range Reconnaissance Imager on NASA New Horizons acquired images of the Pluto field three days apart in late September 2006, in order to see Pluto motion against a dense background of stars.

reference.title: Composite of Comet Borrelly Nucleus, Jets, Coma
reference.description: A composite of images from NASA Deep Space 1 spacecraft shows features of comet Borrelly nucleus, dust jets escaping the nucleus and the cloud-like coma of dust and gases surrounding the nucleus.
